Bill number: HB1130
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 341
 By Lowe

 HOUSE BILL 1130

 By Farmer

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to school counselors.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a)

 (1) Subject to appropriation, the department shall allocate to each LEA

 sufficient funds for the LEA to employ one (1) full-time licensed professional

 school counselor position at each high school in the LEA that enrolls at least six

 hundred (600) students in grades ten through twelve (10-12).

 (2) If an LEA employs one (1) or more part-time licensed professional

 school counselors at a high school that enrolls at least six hundred (600)

 students in grades ten through twelve (10-12), then the LEA may use any funds

 received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to employ the part-time licensed

 professional school counselor on a full-time basis. An LEA that converts a part-

 time licensed professional school counselor position to a full-time position

 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2) satisfies the requirement in subsection (b).

 (3) If an LEA employs one (1) full-time licensed professional school

 counselor for every two hundred fifty (250) student members of the LEA, then the

 LEA may use any funds received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to supplant the

 cost to the LEA of employing the number of full-time licensed professional school

 counselors required to meet the specified ratio.

 (b) Each LEA shall employ one (1) full-time licensed professional school

counselor at each high school for which the LEA receives funding pursuant to this

section. This subsection (b) does not require an LEA that employs one (1) full-time

licensed professional school counselor position for every two hundred fifty (250) student

members of the LEA to employ any additional full-time licensed professional school

counselor positions beyond the number required for the LEA to meet the specified ratio.

 (c) The funds allocated to an LEA pursuant to this section are in addition to the

funds allocated to the LEA for purposes of the TISA.

 (d)

 (1) The state board may promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the roles and responsibilities required of a full-time

 licensed professional school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this

 section that exceed those required of school counselors in § 49-6-303.

 (2) The state board shall promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the amount of time each full-time licensed professional

 school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this section must dedicate

 to providing high school students the preventative and developmental counseling

 services required in § 49-6-303(b), one (1) or more of the counseling and

 guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and any of the services required to

 comply with any additional roles and responsibilities established by the state

 board pursuant to subdivision (d)(1); provided, that each full-time licensed

 professional school counselor must dedicate at least seventy percent (70%) of

 the counselor's time to working directly with high school students.

 SECTION 2. This act is not an appropriation of funds, and funds shall not be obligated

or expended pursuant to this act unless the funds are specifically appropriated by the general

assembly.

 SECTION 3. For purposes of promulgating rules, this act takes effect upon becoming a

law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, this act takes effect July 1, 2025, the

public welfare requiring it, and applies to the 2025-2026 school year and each school year

thereafter.
</bill_text>

<summary>
Subject to an appropriation, the bill would require the state department to provide each local education agency (LEA) enough additional funding to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each of its high schools enrolling at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12. An LEA could use the money to make an existing part-time counselor full-time; doing so would meet the staffing requirement. An LEA that already employs one full-time counselor for every 250 student members could use the funding to cover the cost of counselors needed to meet that ratio, and would not have to hire additional counselors beyond that number. The funding would be in addition to the LEA’s funding for TISA.

The State Board of Education would have authority to set additional roles and responsibilities for counselors funded under the bill. It would be required to set how much time those counselors must spend on specified counseling and guidance services and any additional duties set by the board. At least 70% of each counselor’s time would have to be spent working directly with high school students.

The bill would not itself appropriate money; no funds could be committed or spent under it unless the General Assembly specifically appropriated them. The rulemaking provisions would take effect when the bill became law. The other provisions would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply beginning with the 2025–2026 school year.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: Subject to an appropriation, the bill would require the state department to provide each local education agency (LEA) enough additional funding to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each of its high schools enrolling at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the department’s funding obligation, appropriation condition, counselor qualifications, and school enrollment threshold.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA could use the money to make an existing part-time counselor full-time; doing so would meet the staffing requirement.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the permitted conversion and its satisfaction of the staffing requirement, with the eligible schools and counselor qualifications established in the preceding sentence.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA that already employs one full-time counselor for every 250 student members could use the funding to cover the cost of counselors needed to meet that ratio, and would not have to hire additional counselors beyond that number.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the existing staffing ratio condition and permission to cover the costs of counselors needed to meet it.

assessments.summary_quote: An LEA that already employs one full-time counselor for every 250 student members could use the funding to cover the cost of counselors needed to meet that ratio, and would not have to hire additional counselors beyond that number.
assessments.rationale: Fully conveys the ratio-based exception, but the summary does not clearly state the separate obligation for each LEA to employ a counselor at every high school for which it receives funding.

assessments.summary_quote: The funding would be in addition to the LEA’s funding for TISA.
assessments.rationale: Expressly states that the funding supplements TISA allocations.

assessments.summary_quote: The State Board of Education would have authority to set additional roles and responsibilities for counselors funded under the bill.
assessments.rationale: Conveys discretionary authority to establish additional duties for funded counselors, but omits consultation with the department and does not identify existing statutory duties as the baseline.

assessments.summary_quote: It would be required to set how much time those counselors must spend on specified counseling and guidance services and any additional duties set by the board. At least 70% of each counselor’s time would have to be spent working directly with high school students.
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory time-allocation rules and the 70% direct-service minimum, but omits departmental consultation and the required preventative and developmental services and selection of one or more listed counseling and guidance services.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would not itself appropriate money; no funds could be committed or spent under it unless the General Assembly specifically appropriated them.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both the absence of an appropriation and the restriction on obligating or spending funds without a specific legislative appropriation.

assessments.summary_quote: The rulemaking provisions would take effect when the bill became law.
assessments.rationale: Correctly conveys the immediate effective date for rulemaking purposes.

assessments.summary_quote: The other provisions would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply beginning with the 2025–2026 school year.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the effective date for other purposes and ongoing application starting with the specified school year.
